case_studies.title: Switchcraft: AI Model Router for Agentic Tool Calling
case_studies.abstract: Agentic AI systems that invoke external tools are powerful but costly, leading developers to default to large models and overspend inference budgets. Model routing can mitigate this, but existing routers are designed for chat completion rather than tool use. We present Switchcraft, the first (to the best of our knowledge) model router optimized for agentic tool calling. Switchcraft operates inline, selecting the lowest-cost model subject to correctness. We construct an evaluation framework on five function-calling benchmarks and train a DistilBERT-based classifier, deployed under a latency bud
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of costly AI model invocation by building Switchcraft, a model router that selects the lowest-cost model while ensuring correctness, resulting in optimized agentic tool calling. Switchcraft operates inline and is optimized for tool use, not just chat completion. This research may help reduce costs for AI-powered systems that rely on external tools.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered systems that invoke external tools, here is what to do: review your current model invocation process, consider implementing a model router like Switchcraft, and evaluate its potential to reduce inference budgets and latency. This flags a risk: if your organization uses large models and overspends inference budgets, check your model invocation process immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to AI and machine learning infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: Model router for agentic tool calling is a new concept, but it's applied in a way relevant to IT engineers. The tool and systems mentioned, such as DistilBERT and latency budgets, are directly relevant to the IT audience. case_studies.title: Dooly: Configuration-Agnostic, Redundancy-Aware Profiling for LLM Inference Simulation
case_studies.abstract: Selecting the optimal LLM inference configuration requires evaluation across hardware, serving engines, attention backends, and model architectures, since no single choice performs best across all workloads. Profile-based simulators are the standard tool, yet they hardcode their operation set to a specific configuration and re-profile every operation from scratch, making exploration prohibitively expensive. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimal LLM inference configuration selection by building a configuration-agnostic profiling tool called Dooly, which resulted in more efficient evaluation of different configurations. Dooly allows for simulation of various hardware and model architectures without requiring re-profiling from scratch. This can help reduce the cost and time of exploring different configurations.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage LLM inference workloads, here is what to do: review your current profiling tools and consider adopting Dooly or similar configuration-agnostic solutions to optimize your configuration selection process. This flags a risk: if your organization uses hard-coded profile-based simulators, check for potential inefficiencies in your current workflow. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work outside of LLM inference.

case_studies.title: VibeServe: Can AI Agents Build Bespoke LLM Serving Systems?
case_studies.abstract: For years, we have built LLM serving systems like any other critical infrastructure: a single general-purpose stack, hand-tuned over many engineer-years, meant to support every model and workload. In this paper, we take the opposite bet: a multi-agent loop that automatically synthesizes bespoke serving systems for different usage scenarios. We propose VibeServe, the first agentic loop that generates entire LLM serving stacks end-to-end. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of inefficient large language model serving systems by building VibeServe, an AI-powered system that automatically synthesizes bespoke serving systems for different usage scenarios, resulting in optimized performance. VibeServe uses a multi-agent loop to generate entire serving stacks end-to-end. The system aims to reduce the need for manual tuning and support various models and workloads.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage large language model serving systems, here is what to do: assess your current system's performance, consider implementing VibeServe to automate the synthesis of bespoke serving systems, and evaluate the potential benefits of optimized performance for your organization. This flags a risk: if your org uses general-purpose LLM serving stacks, check for potential inefficiencies and consider alternatives. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those managing LLM serving systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper does not discuss monetisation potential or practical applications of VibeServe, such as proposing a service to a client or building a revenue-generating product.

case_studies.title: Coding Agents Don't Know When to Act
case_studies.abstract: Coding agents are increasingly deployed to autonomously maintain software, including to resolve user-reported issues: a bug report comes in and the agent creates a patch to address it. However, in any real-world deployment, they will encounter stale bug reports about issues that have already been resolved. Agents should recognize this and abstain from modifying the code to avoid accumulating technical debt. To systematically evaluate whether current agents do so, we introduce FixedBench, a code benchmark with 200 human-verified coding tasks in which no code changes are required, testing five r
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of coding agents unnecessarily modifying code for already resolved issues, the authors built a benchmark called FixedBench to test this, and the result shows that current agents do not perform well in this scenario. The benchmark consists of 200 human-verified coding tasks that require no code changes. This research aims to improve the efficiency of coding agents in real-world deployments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage automated coding agents, here is what to do: review your agents' performance in handling stale bug reports, check if they can recognize already resolved issues, and consider using a benchmark like FixedBench to evaluate their performance. This flags a risk: if your organization uses coding agents to resolve user-reported issues, check their ability to abstain from modifying code when no changes are required immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those managing automated coding agents.
case_studies.relevance_tag: IT infrastructure, software engineering, AI deployment
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper explores the issue of stale bug reports affecting coding agents, and proposes a benchmark to evaluate their performance. This has high IT relevance as it directly affects how coding agents are deployed in software maintenance. High novelty as the problem and potential solution is not widely known or discussed. case_studies.title: On Time, Within Budget: Constraint-Driven Online Resource Allocation for Agentic Workflows
case_studies.abstract: Agentic systems increasingly solve complex user requests by executing orchestrated workflows, where subtasks are assigned to specialized models or tools and coordinated according to their dependencies. While recent work improves agent efficiency by optimizing the performance--cost--latency frontier, real deployments often impose concrete requirements: a workflow must be completed within a specified budget and before a specified deadline. This shifts the goal from average efficiency optimization to maximizing the probability that the entire workflow completes successfully under explicit budget
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of managing complex workflows within a specified budget and deadline. The authors built a system that allocates resources online to maximize the probability of successful workflow completion. The result is a more efficient way to manage workflows under explicit budget and time constraints.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud-based workflows, here is what to do: review your current resource allocation strategy, consider implementing a constraint-driven approach to optimize workflow completion within budget and time constraints, and assess the potential benefits of this new method for your organization.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Agentic systems, workflows, and optimization are related to IT infrastructure and deployment, especially given real-world constraints. However, the paper may assume existing infrastructure rather than proposing novel solutions. Forwarding it to a colleague might elicit a response due to novelty in optimization under budget constraints.

case_studies.title: Abductive Reasoning with Probabilistic Commonsense
case_studies.abstract: Recent efforts to improve the reasoning abilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) have focused on integrating formal logic solvers within neurosymbolic frameworks. A key challenge is that formal solvers lack commonsense world knowledge, preventing them from making reasoning steps that humans find obvious. Prior methods address this by using LLMs to supply missing commonsense assumptions, but these approaches implicitly assume universal agreement on such commonsense facts. In reality, commonsense beliefs vary across individuals. We propose a probabilistic framework for abductive commonsense rea
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of integrating formal logic solvers with real-world commonsense knowledge in Large Language Models. The authors built a probabilistic framework for abductive commonsense reasoning, allowing for more human-like decision-making. The result is a more advanced reasoning ability in language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving language models and reasoning abilities in artificial intelligence.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel probabilistic framework for abductive commonsense reasoning in LLMs, but direct relevance to IT infrastructure is low. Could be applicable in 90 days if adapted for use in IT workflows.

case_studies.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling
case_studies.abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) has become an effective approach for improving large language model performance by allocating additional computation during inference. However, existing TTS strategies are largely hand-crafted: researchers manually design reasoning patterns and tune heuristics by intuition, leaving much of the computation-allocation space unexplored. We propose an environment-driven framework, AutoTTS, that changes what researchers design: from individual TTS heuristics to environments where TTS strategies can be discovered automatically. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of manually designing test-time scaling strategies for large language models by building an environment-driven framework called AutoTTS. The result is a framework that can automatically discover and optimize test-time scaling strategies, potentially improving language model performance. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: The Memory Curse: How Expanded Recall Erodes Cooperative Intent in LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: Context window expansion is often treated as a straightforward capability upgrade for LLMs, but we find it systematically fails in multi-agent social dilemmas. Across 7 LLMs and 4 games over 500 rounds, expanding accessible history degrades cooperation in 18 of 28 model--game settings, a pattern we term the memory curse. We isolate the underlying mechanism through three analyses. The result showed that expanding accessible history degrades cooperation in most model-game settings. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Self-Play Enhancement via Advantage-Weighted Refinement in Online Federated LLM Fine-Tuning with Real-Time Feedback
case_studies.abstract: Recent works have advanced feedback-based learning systems, whereby a foundation model is able to intake incoming feedback (e.g., a user) to self-improve, creating a self-loop system of training. However, existing works are limited in needing to consider an offline setup to allow for such feedback-based methods, and are further limited in the need of requiring privileged ground-truth contexts for training. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of limited feedback-based learning systems by building a self-loop system of training that can incorporate real-time feedback from users. The authors built an online federated learning system that refines foundation models using advantage-weighted refinement. The result is a more effective and efficient way to fine-tune large language models.
